key_insight: Light can reversibly switch halide ions in 2D mixed-halide perovskites through strong light-lattice coupling, not defects, enabling a defect-free self-resetting photoresponse.
engineering_relevance: This points to a route for tunable, reversible optoelectronic devices and photo-switchable materials with improved stability and recoverability.
method: Nudged elastic band calculations mapped the halide-exchange activation pathway.
Photo-force calculations showed light-induced non-equilibrium work driving partial ion motion.
GW plus lattice-dynamics analysis linked optical redshift and soft phonons to the excited-state mechanism.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the calculated optical absorption matches experiment in the dark, and light produces a clear redshift consistent with bandgap renormalization and reversible halide swapping.
watch_item: The mechanism appears to only partially overcome the activation barrier under illumination, so practical switching speed, durability, and operating-light requirements may limit device implementation.
paper_title: Reversible photo-switching optical functionality in two-dimensional mixed-halide hybrid perovskites
